findings.summary: The pinned-lease command is split across two lines with no continuation, so it is broken as written.
findings.evidence: "git push --force-with-lease=" followed on the next line by "  feat:<expected-sha>" (no trailing backslash)
findings.fix: Write it as one line: `git push --force-with-lease=feat:<expected-sha>`, or end the first line with ` \`. The `=` must be followed immediately by the value.

findings.summary: The code block runs `git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD` alongside `range-diff` as if it were a routine inspection step, and `patch-id` is used without explanation.
findings.evidence: Code: "git range-diff main..ORIG_HEAD \\ main..HEAD / git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD / ls .git/rebase-merge/" with the note "range-diff compares old and new". Bullet: "Same ==patch-id== already upstream? Skipped automatically".
findings.fix: Remove the reset line from this block, or label it "undo, discards the rebase result". Define patch-id in one clause, e.g. "a hash of the diff content, so identical changes match even with different SHAs".

findings.summary: The page says autosquash only reorders the todo, but it also rewrites the action keywords. This contradicts step 3 on the same page, which says it flips pick to fixup/squash.

findings.evidence: Callout: "Fetch first, rebase second, lease-push last." The diagram ends with "verify" after "lease push", while the code reads the log before pushing. Mistake bullet: "IDE auto-fetch silently defeats the lease", with only "Lease checks remote == your last fetch" given earlier.
